chunks: And as for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from some of our companions from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"The Sa'iba and the non-Sa'iba are equal in manumission."

The first point regarding it is that it is Mursal (disconnected), and its manner is such that it is not to be opposed by the Musnad (connected) reports. The second point is that in the apparent meaning of the report, it is not stated that the Wilayah (manumission right) of the Sa'iba is like the Wilayah of the non-Sa'iba; rather, it made them equal in manumission (Al-'Itq). And we say with that, so from where is it that they do not differ in the Wilayah?
And that which reveals what we mentioned, also, is what was narrated:

key_terms.اَلسَّائِبَةُ: A specific category of freed slave in Islamic law
key_terms.اَلْأَخْبَارُ اَلْمُسْنَدَةُ: Musnad reports; narrations with a complete, connected chain of narrators
key_terms.اَلْعِتْقِ: Manumission or freeing of a slave
key_terms.اَلْوَلاَءِ: Wilayah; the right of manumission or patronage
key_terms.مُرْسَلٌ: Mursal; a hadith where a companion narrates directly from the Prophet without mentioning the intermediate tabi'i

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Sa'iba and non-Sa'iba in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi critically analyzes this report from Zurara to demonstrate that the equality of the 'Sa'iba' (freed slave) applies specifically to the act of manumission rather than the right of 'Wilayah' (patronage), thereby distinguishing it from explicitly linked narrations. This nuanced interpretation highlights the Shia scholarly method of differentiating between the legal act of freeing and the subsequent inheritance of patronage rights, ensuring consistency with established juristic principles.
